findings.detail: ClientSpace embeds the real object cache: GetObject returns the actual SmartBlock; Remove(ctx,id) returns the original error; Storage returns ClientSpaceStorage with native TreeStorage/AnyStore. Objecttree.Storage.Root/GetAfterAddSeq/Heads signatures match the fixture. The owned selector uses actual service.spaceControllers under s.mu, SpaceId, Current, loader.LoadWaiter and exact loaded Space identity. No substitute Space/controller or product RPC was introduced.

The target and private host are captured before barriers. The original native append owns settings/target/private locks before append-before-native. Both original Remove calls transition their exact cache values to Closing before the real controller is closed. Identity-bound deadline events require both entries to exhaust the unchanged original ten-second cache pass. An active private entry cannot mask the intended downstream settings fence.

Initial append barrier precedes original AddContentWithValidator and final ACL hold. Closing can therefore pass aclObjectManager teardown. The settings attempt targets the same actual reserved settings object held by the lease. The fixture requires cache Close return before this attempt and rejects settings completion/storage close before commit. Original AddAll is forwarded once with its original context/changes/heads/snapshot and exact error. The post-AddAll barrier precedes ACL release and target/settings unlock; raw native history is read while these original locks still fence teardown.

The two-entry genesis+seed raw hash map and exact head are recorded, re-read unchanged while close is blocked, then compared entry-by-entry to the three-entry durable map. The sole new head/change ID is bound to the unchanged CREATED generated response. Cold phase native read requires LOCAL_VERIFIED_TREE, the same heads, two exact persisted protobuf claims, no conflicts and no pending observed IDs.

The raced append request is marshalled once and forwarded by original generated byte entry. Original bytes/hash are retained in private state through account shutdown. Reopen forwards exactly those bytes once, requires ALREADY_EXISTS_SAME_PAYLOAD, the same claim, empty ChangeId, exact claim equality and fully equal before/after native read including local watermark; all raw hashes and heads remain unchanged.

On the success route all append/remover/controller goroutines are joined before ending capture. Capture failure cleanup is registered after ordinary account shutdown cleanup, so it releases its own bounded gates first without releasing any native lock or fabricating native results. Both explicit AccountStop/GetApp-nil and AppShutdown are required before PASS output/state retention. The original loaded controller route permits subsequent ordinary idempotent application shutdown and avoids a direct double clientspace cache Close.

Observer records only selected stage/ID/pointer identity and OK/ERROR; it does no app callback, authorization, context replacement, retry or native lock manipulation. Fifteen exact events, no duplicates, all eight pointer identity pairs, strict partial order and no timeout/cancellation/overflow are mandatory. All dynamic identities passed here are concrete native pointers; interface comparisons are valid for this fixture.

format_scope: Root exact-byte gofmt/idempotence receipt reviewed; this is not an independent native compilation.
scope: Only the frozen ten Go compile-composition files, exact seven-file instrumentation patch, native API and fixture lifetime/history/retained-request semantics. Evolving Python controller/materializer/workflow excluded.
scope_notes: The observation key original_controller_close_calls=1 denotes the explicit raced selector forwarding. Ordinary AccountStop later invokes its normal controller shutdown path again; this is not a claim of one total controller.Close invocation for the account process.

Race and reopen are separate phase entry points. The still-unreviewed controller must require two distinct real process IDs, an unchanged binary/source/nonce/account/fixture binding and exact retained private state. This source review alone does not prove a cold process occurred.

The native source uses a seeded existing private root; first-root installation, account switching, settings deletion, duplicate Close completion and new-engine parity remain outside this runtime case.

SmartBlock.Close has original upstream behavior including discarded source.Close return; the fixture accepts only the observed original Remove result and does not claim it added observation of every internal unexposed error.
No speculative product lifecycle fix is justified or introduced. The proposed run must actually reach both deadline events and same-object settings fence; failing coverage is not PASS.
